question: In a routine analysis of a 59-year-old woman, smoker of 20 cigarettes / day for 25 years, a hypercalcemia of 11.3 mg / dL was detected with a phosphorus of 3.4 mg / dL. It would NOT be efficient to enter:

options.opb: Determine serum levels of vitamin D.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hypercalcemia" -> "Possible primary hyperparathyroidism" -> "Determine serum levels of PTH" -> "Efficient" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Hypercalcemia" -> "Possible vitamin D intoxication" -> "Determine serum levels of vitamin D" -> "Efficient" -> 85%

analysis: In the context of hypercalcemia, it is important to determine the underlying cause. Common causes include primary hyperparathyroidism and malignancy-related hypercalcemia. Determining serum levels of PTH and vitamin D can help differentiate between these causes. A chest X-ray can be useful to identify potential lung malignancies, especially in a smoker, which could cause hypercalcemia through paraneoplastic syndromes. Hydroxyprolinuria is not a standard or efficient test in the initial evaluation of hypercalcemia, as it is more related to bone turnover and not directly helpful in diagnosing the cause of hypercalcemia in this context.
